newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican army forces end to oil well blockade.
newsitem.headline: Mexican army forces end to oil well blockade.

text.p: Soldiers on Friday forcibly removed peasants from oil wells they were blockading in the eastern state of Tabasco, and at least 10 protestors were injured in the crackdown, witnesses said.

Jose Antonio de la O, a local leader of the opposition Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), said he witnessed some 300 members of the army and federal police violently dislodge the protestors on the 25th day of the blockade.
He said eight peasants were arrested in the operation at Centla, some 20 miles (35 km) outside the Tabasco state capital of Villahermosa.

Authorities insisted the operation was carried out with a minimum of violence, and followed a request from state oil company Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) to put a stop to the protests at three of its oil drilling wells.

Peasants, many linked to the leftist PRD, have frequently seized wells in Tabasco, disrupting production. They have protested environmental damage to their crops and livelihoods, and also sought cash compensation from Pemex.
